title: Sharp product small-set expansion
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$ coordinates, and let $0<\lambda<1/2$. Suppose every coordinate atom has probability at least $\lambda$, and let $q>2$ and $\rho\ge 0$ satisfy $\rho\le r_q(\lambda)^2$, where $r_q(\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(u/q)/\sinh\bigl(u/(q/(q-1))\bigr)}$ and $u=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. Then for every event $A$ in the outcome space, $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(\mathbf{1}_A)\le\Pr_P(A)^{2-2/q}$.
hypotheses_covered: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite product probability space $P$ with $n$ coordinates
Every coordinate atom has probability at least $\lambda$
An event $A$ in the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda<1/2$, and let $q>2$. Define $r_q(\lambda)=\sqrt{\frac{\sinh(\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)/q)}{\sinh(\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)/(q/(q-1)))}}$; if $0\le\rho\le r_q(\lambda)^2$, then $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(\mathbf1_A)\le\Pr_P(A)^{2-2/q}$ for every event $A\subseteq\Omega$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\operatorname{Stab}_a(h)=\mathbb E_P[hT_a h]$; $\Pr_P(A)=\mathbb E_P\mathbf1_A$, where $\mathbf1_A$ is $1$ on $A$ and $0$ elsewhere. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
